findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Name the 'typed fit/context error' (existing type to reuse or a new errors.py subclass) so AC 4's oversize-input test and any type-based routing have a concrete class to assert against.
evidence: Plan: 'Authoritative input (system/user/tool) that cannot fit fails closed with a typed fit/context error — never shortened.'
AC 4: 'Authoritative-input overflow raises the typed fit/context failure ... verified by an oversize-input test.'

src/rebar/llm/errors.py hierarchy has LLMConfigError, StructuredOutputError, UnretryableOutputError, LLMBudgetExhaustedError — none named for a fit/context/window-overflow condition, and Scope's pai_retry.py bullet lists no new error type.
ABSENCE: an executor writing the oversize-input test cannot tell whether to reuse an existing type or add a new one, nor what name/module to assert against.
findings.finding: The 'typed fit/context error' that authoritative-input overflow must raise (Approach item 1; AC line 4) is referenced but its type is never named — errors.py defines no fit/context error and Scope introduces no new type name.
findings.location: Approach item 1 ('fails closed with a typed fit/context error'); Acceptance Criteria line 4 ('raises the typed fit/context failure')
scenarios: Writing the oversize-input acceptance test: which exception class does it assert?
Downstream except-handler routing (interpret_failure) that keys on exception TYPE, not message — an unnamed type risks being caught as a generic StructuredOutputError and misrouted.
findings.suggested_fix: In Scope (pai_retry.py) and Approach item 1, name the exact exception class raised on authoritative-input overflow — e.g. a new `LLMContextOverflowError(LLMRunnerError)` in errors.py, or an explicit reuse of an existing type — and reference it in AC 4.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State explicitly that the UsageLimits.request_limit output-retry addend equals the same N used in retries={"output": N} (both derived from structured.OUTPUT_RETRIES lowered by req.structured_retry_limit), and pin that equality in the budget test so the two limits cannot diverge.
evidence: Plan: 'build_usage_limits sets the operation-wide UsageLimits.request_limit = base allowance (ceil(eff_max_iter/2)) PLUS the configured output-retry allowance'
Plan: 'one budget = retries={"output": N} (structured.OUTPUT_RETRIES=2, lowered by req.structured_retry_limit)'

The plan never states the request-budget addend == N; each in-run output/concision retry costs one request against request_limit (pydantic-ai request_limit counts model requests), so addend < N under-provisions the shared request budget

AC line 5: 'length/max_tokens consumes at most the configured output-retry allowance (shared with parse/validation retries)' — the shared cap is only exact if request-budget addend and output-retry N are the same number
findings.finding: The plan configures two independent limits that must agree — the request-budget addend (UsageLimits.request_limit = base + 'the configured output-retry allowance') and retries={'output': N} (N = OUTPUT_RETRIES lowered by req.structured_retry_limit) — but never states that the request addend equals N. If the addend is smaller than N, a legitimate parse/validation or concision ModelRetry consumes a request and can trip request_limit before the output-retry counter is exhausted, aborting the run early despite unused output budget.
findings.location: Approach step 3 (One shared request budget, one shared retry counter) / Scope (build_usage_limits) / AC line 5
scenarios: req.structured_retry_limit lowers N while the request addend stays at a fixed constant, or vice-versa, so the two limits diverge and the operation aborts on request_limit mid-retry with output budget still nominally available
An invalid-then-valid case (AC #1) needs 2 requests but the request addend was set below N, tripping the request limit before the second (valid) attempt
findings.suggested_fix: In build_usage_limits, compute the output allowance once as the SAME N passed to retries={"output": N} (OUTPUT_RETRIES lowered by req.structured_retry_limit) and add exactly that N to request_limit; assert request_limit == base + N and retries["output"] == N in the budget/source-census test.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Have pai_retry's operation guard COMPOSE (wrap/call) the shared S1 delegation body rather than re-implement the check_response / UnretryableOutputError / StructuredOutputError→ModelRetry tail, so the only new code is the truncation→concision reclassification prepended before it.
evidence: Plan step 2(b): 'otherwise it delegates to the SAME S1 logic — structured.check_response(response), re-raise terminal UnretryableOutputError (refusal/content_filter) and translate a retryable StructuredOutputError (transient error) into ModelRetry'
pai_output.py:70-82 — `_StructuredResponseGuard.after_model_request` already implements exactly this try/except delegation

The plan's stated reason for a separate capability is 'attached INSTEAD OF pai_output.guard_capability(), whose terminal contract is UNCHANGED for other callers until S5' — a reason to not MODIFY S1, not a reason to COPY its body
findings.finding: The new `pai_retry` operation guard re-implements the refusal/content_filter/transient-error delegation tail that S1's landed `pai_output.guard_capability()` already provides; only the truncation→concision `ModelRetry` reclassification is genuinely new. The delegation body (call `structured.check_response`, re-raise `UnretryableOutputError`, translate `StructuredOutputError`→`ModelRetry`) is identical to `_StructuredResponseGuard.after_model_request` (pai_output.py:70-82).
scenarios: A future fix to the refusal/content_filter delegation semantics must be applied in two places (pai_output.guard_capability and pai_retry's guard) that will silently drift
S5 cutover reconciling the two guards inherits divergent copies of the same delegation logic
findings.suggested_fix: Factor the shared delegation tail into a single helper (e.g. reuse pai_output's internal check-and-translate, or extract it) that BOTH guards call; pai_retry's guard adds only the length/max_tokens two-layer inspection + concision ModelRetry ahead of that shared call.
